summary: Nia Smith brings her sophomore EP to our ears for us tap into her Growth from love, loss, self-worth and outgrowing people.
title: Payback is A Dog (EP)
content:
Nia Smith absolutely gave us a solid project with this one, she's adding so much value to the R&B scene in the UK. I remember the first time listening to this project and thinking to myself:

> Who is this Nia Smith and why does she sound so tuff? Surely, she's been around for some years and I haven't tapped in properly.

Well, it is safe to say I was wrong with that assumption in my head.

 \
With Payback Is A Dog, Nia Smith sounds less like an artist trying to prove herself and more like one who has grown comfortable trusting her own creative instincts (in my own Opinion: Artists from the UK rarely show this kind of trait). There is a noticeable sense of confidence throughout the project, particularly in the way she approaches its production, songwriting and emotional direction. Her sound feels laidback and effortless, yet there is enough substance beneath the surface to keep the listener engaged. Rather than relying on overly complicated arrangements or forcing memorable moments, Nia allows the music to breathe, giving her vocals and lyrical delivery room to take centre stage.

What I particularly appreciate about the EP is its balance between vulnerability and self-assurance. There is a refreshing honesty in the way she explores relationships, personal growth and the emotional consequences of letting people go. Nothing feels excessively forced or overproduced. Instead, the project carries a natural sense of maturity, making it an enjoyable and, at times, introspective listen.

Ultimately, Payback Is A Dog feels like a confident step forward for Nia Smith. It is the kind of project that doesn't necessarily demand your attention but gradually earns it through its laidback atmosphere, thoughtful songwriting and understated emotional depth. Big difference.

My three favorite Tracks from the project have to be:

High, Limit and Tough (feat. DESTIN CONRAD)
verdict:
I was so impressed to a point that I had to put her first EP on my radar for a listen.
If she continues on this type of artistry, she has to become a big name in the UK scene.
Definitely one for the future.
